stories.hook: ¿Puede el ketamina rivalizar con la terapia electroconvulsiva?
stories.headline: Ketamina muestra eficacia comparable a la ECT en depresión no psicótica
stories.finding: El ketamina, antagonista del NMDAR, produce una respuesta antidepresiva rápida y más tolerable que los antidepresivos tradicionales. En un ensayo comparativo, su eficacia fue similar a la de la terapia electroconvulsiva en pacientes con depresión no psicótica.
stories.takeaway: Este dato sugiere que el ketamina puede ser una alternativa eficaz y menos invasiva a la ECT, ampliando opciones de tratamiento rápido para la depresión resistente.
stories.paperTitle: Neuropharmacology of Ketamine and Its Use in the Treatment of Major Depressive Disorder: A Review
stories.originalAbstract: Depression is a common yet potentially debilitating mood disorder with complex neurobiological underpinnings, including deficiencies in monoaminergic and glutamatergic signaling, overactivity of the lateral habenula, and dysregulation of brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF) signaling. Ketamine has emerged as a mechanistically novel, effective, and rapidly acting antidepressant. Ketamine's primary effects are due to N-methyl-D-aspartate receptor (NMDAR) antagonism, although hypotheses regarding the importance of its impact on monoaminergic signaling (preclinical evidence), BDNF signaling (preclinical evidence), opioid receptor agonism (preclinical evidence), and neuroinflammation (clinical evidence) have gained traction. Compared to selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs) and tricyclic antidepressants (TCAs), ketamine demonstrates greater efficacy, a significantly faster onset of action, and generally more tolerable side effects. However, its benefits are offset by a far shorter duration of antidepressant effects and accessibility limitations. In a head-to-head trial, compared to electroconvulsive therapy (ECT), ketamine showed similar efficacy in non-psychotic depression while providing clinically significant relief more rapidly. While promising, further research is needed to optimize ketamine's dosing regimen, enhance its accessibility, and better understand potential drawbacks such as bladder toxicity and addiction potential. Additionally, studying the mechanisms behind ketamine's antidepressant action may provide deeper insight into the neurobiology of depression.

stories.hook: ¿Por qué la ansiedad sanitaria distorsiona la interpretación?
stories.headline: Sesgo interpretativo exclusivo de amenazas de salud vinculado a la rumiación negativa
stories.finding: En una muestra comunitaria de 124 personas con ansiedad sanitaria elevada, se observó un sesgo interpretativo que favorecía estímulos amenazantes para la salud, pero no para estímulos de ansiedad general, disforia o positivos. Además, la rumiación negativa explicó parcialmente esta asociación.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo sugiere que la intervención clínica en ansiedad sanitaria debe focalizarse en modificar la rumiación y los sesgos específicos de interpretación, lo que podría prevenir la escalada de la preocupación por la salud.
stories.paperTitle: Specificity of computationally modeled interpretation biases in health anxiety and the contributions of repetitive negative thinking in a community sample of individuals with elevated health anxiety
stories.originalAbstract: Cognitive-behavioral models of health anxiety suggest interpretation biases for ambiguous information play a role in its etiology. This study sought to clarify how specific these biases are in health anxiety and how other potential causal processes, like repetitive negative thinking (RNT), are associated with interpretation biases and health anxiety. Participants from the community (N = 124) with at least mildly elevated levels of health anxiety (Short Health Anxiety Inventory scores ≥ 18) completed a self-report questionnaire assessing repetitive negative thinking (RNT), as well as an interpretation bias task based on the Word Sentence Association paradigm. Task outcomes were computationally modelled using drift diffusion modeling and interpretation bias was operationalized as drift rate, i.e., the rate of evidence accumulation to decide between two choices (in this case, the emotional interpretation or the benign interpretation). Results showed that individuals with health anxiety exhibit interpretation biases specific to health-threatening stimuli but not general anxiety, dysphoric, or positive stimuli. In addition, RNT partially explained the association between interpretation biases for health anxiety-related stimuli and health anxiety symptom severity. Our work suggests health anxiety-specific interpretation biases and repetitive negative thinking may be important targets for intervention, whether through psychotherapy or computerized interventions (e.g., cognitive bias modification).

stories.hook: ¿Dos ataques son suficientes para predecir futuros pánicos?
stories.headline: Modelos personalizados predicen ataques de pánico con solo dos eventos previos.
stories.finding: En una muestra longitudinal de 42 estudiantes, 20 modelos personalizados alcanzaron un PR AUC medio de 0.85, superando modelos basados en auto‑reporte. Solo se necesitaron dos ataques de pánico para que el modelo alcanzara un rendimiento adecuado.
stories.takeaway: Esta evidencia sugiere que la monitorización continua con wearables permite intervenciones tempranas y personalizadas, reduciendo la carga clínica de los ataques de pánico.
stories.paperTitle: Development of personalized machine learning models for predicting panic attacks in college students
stories.originalAbstract: Panic attacks (PAs) are unexpected episodes of intense fear and anxiety, accompanied by cognitive and physical symptoms that significantly impair day-to-day functioning. This study proposes a machine learning approach to predict PA risk in individuals across mental health conditions, enabling timely and potentially preventive mental health intervention. We demonstrate the efficacy of the approach in a longitudinal sample of behavioral and physiological data collected using Oura rings from 42 college students over six months. Of personalized models, 20 achieved performance significantly better than random chance with a mean PR AUC of 0.85, outperforming those based on self-reported distress scores (mean PR AUC = 0.79 for n=21) and self-reported daily stressor counts (mean PR AUC = 0.94 for only n=7), which both require active user engagement. Low Jaccard similarity (12.6%) of key features for predicting PAs across personalized Oura models, and lower performance of the generalized cohort model (PR AUC = 0.40), further supports the need for personalized modeling approaches. Post-hoc analyses of personalized models suggest that only two PAs are needed to enable suitable model performance. Notably, for the 22 personalized Oura models with poor performance, better than random chance models were identified for nearly all (n=20) through an innovative cross-participant approach. Collectively, findings suggest that passively collected daily measurements of sleep, activity, and physiology can be used to predict PAs and could be leveraged to identify individually tailored lifestyle interventions for reducing PA risk.

stories.hook: ¿Puede una IA personalizar la terapia y reducir el estrés?
stories.headline: Una herramienta digital generativa disminuye significativamente el estrés frente a un control de reestructuración cognitiva
stories.finding: En un ensayo preregistrado con 237 participantes, el sistema GUIDE redujo significativamente el estrés (p = .02) y mejoró la experiencia de usuario (p = .04) en comparación con un control basado en LLM para reestructuración cognitiva. Además, facilitó diversas formas de reflexión y acción mediante flujos de interacción variables.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo sugiere que la generación en tiempo real de contenidos y formatos de interacción puede potenciar la efectividad de intervenciones cognitivo-conductuales digitales, ofreciendo una vía para personalizar no solo el contenido sino la experiencia terapéutica.
stories.paperTitle: Generative Experiences for Digital Mental Health Interventions: Evidence from a Randomized Study
stories.journal: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology (UIST)
stories.originalAbstract: Digital mental health (DMH) tools have extensively explored personalization of interventions to users’ needs and contexts. However, this personalization often targets what support is provided, not how it is experienced. Even well-matched content can fail when the interaction format misaligns with how someone can engage. We introduce generative experience as an approach to DMH support, where the intervention experience is composed at runtime. We instantiate this in GUIDE, a system that generates personalized intervention content and multimodal interaction structure through rubric-guided generation of modular components. In a preregistered study with N=237 participants, GUIDE significantly reduced stress (p=.02) and improved user experience (p=.04) compared to an LLM-based cognitive restructuring control. GUIDE also supported diverse forms of reflection and action through varied interaction flows, while revealing tensions around personalization across the interaction sequence. This work lays the foundation for interventions that dynamically shape how support is experienced and enacted in digital settings.

stories.hook: ¿Los traumas infantiles alteran la percepción de seguridad psicológica?
stories.headline: Los ACE predicen menor neurocepción de seguridad psicológica en adultos
stories.finding: En un estudio transversal con 222 adultos mayores de 20 años, se observó que las experiencias adversas infantiles (ACE) predijeron significativamente una menor neurocepción de seguridad psicológica. Los datos se recopilaron entre enero y julio de 2024 en Lahore, utilizando escalas validadas.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo sugiere que los traumas tempranos pueden comprometer la capacidad de percibir entornos seguros, lo que orienta intervenciones que fortalezcan la neurocepción de seguridad en la terapia de trauma.
stories.paperTitle: Unraveling the Nexus: Investigating the Relationship between Neuroception of Psychological Safety and Childhood Traumas
stories.originalAbstract: This research aims to explore the intricate relationships among neuroception of psychological safety and childhood traumas. Early life experiences, particularly adverse childhood experiences (ACEs), have been shown to impact neurodevelopment and influence later perceptions of psychological safety. This study seeks to build on existing literature by examining these intricate relationships. Analytical cross-sectional design was used to assess the participants at a single point in time. The data gathered throughout Lahore, Punjab from Jan 2024 to July 2024. The sample size of 222 adult participants was selected by the convenience sampling strategy. A diverse sample of adult’s age range of 20 and over recruited to ensure representation of various adult stages, genders, and cultural backgrounds. Assessment of participants was based on established measures and their eligibility for the study was determined accordingly. For assessment purpose three scales were used; Neuroception of Psychological Safety Scale (NPSS) for psychological safety and Adverse Childhood Experiences (ACE) for childhood trauma were used. Adverse childhood experiences measured by ACE to be a significant predictor of neuroception of psychological safety (p<.000) and also significant predictor of all its subscales of social engagement (p<.000), compassion (p<.000) and bodily sensations (p<.000). The results are in line with previous literature linking trauma with Polyvagal theory that Adverse childhood Experiences (ACEs) like violence, physical, emotional and sexual abuse, or being developed with such parents and other family members suffering from the mental health issues or substance abuse history can provide the base for physiological and mental health problems in later life.

stories.hook: ¿Cómo adaptar la interpretación al trauma complejo?
stories.headline: Cinco ejes para una práctica psicoanalítica sensible al trauma
stories.finding: El scoping review de intervenciones psicoanalíticas para trauma y disociación de los últimos 15 años identificó cinco ejes: vulnerabilidad a la desregulación, acceso simbólico limitado, disociación estructural, desorganización en la intimidad y enactments en la relación terapéutica. Se propone calibrar la interpretación según la capacidad regulatoria y simbólica del paciente.
stories.takeaway: Este marco guía a los analistas a ajustar la intervención al nivel regulatorio y simbólico del paciente, mejorando la tolerancia al trauma y evitando interpretaciones prematuras.
stories.paperTitle: Recent trends and adaptations in trauma-informed psychoanalytic psychotherapies: A scoping review.
stories.originalAbstract: A growing sensitivity has emerged within psychoanalytic theory and intervention to the specific conditions of complex posttraumatic pathology and its clinical challenges. Yet an articulated, encompassing view of the diverse proposals within this new sensitivity is still lacking. This article advances such articulation through a scoping review of psychoanalytic interventions focused on trauma and dissociation published over the past 15 years. Our analysis identifies five axes of trauma-sensitive psychoanalytic practice addressing vulnerability to dysregulation, limited symbolic access to traumatic material, structural dissociation, vulnerability to disorganization in contexts of intimacy, and enactments arising around dissociative collusions and dilemmas of recognition within the therapeutic dyad. Overall, the reviewed literature relocates interpretation within a temporally and clinically responsive framework, in which the timing and form of interpretive interventions are calibrated to the traumatized patient's regulatory, dissociative, and symbolic capacities. We conclude by outlining essential aspects of the therapeutic stance implied by these contributions. (PsycInfo Database Record (c) 2026 APA, all rights reserved).

stories.hook: ¿Regulación emocional reduce la agresión? Descubre la evidencia
stories.headline: Estrategias adaptativas de regulación emocional reducen la agresión; estrategias maladaptativas aumentan riesgo
stories.finding: El meta‑análisis incluyó 171 estudios con 252 605 participantes y encontró que el uso de estrategias adaptativas de regulación emocional se asocia con una reducción moderada de la agresión (r = −0.090). En contraste, las estrategias maladaptativas y las dificultades regulativas se relacionan con un aumento de la agresión (r = 0.329 y r = 0.248, respectivamente).
stories.takeaway: Comprender la relación entre regulación emocional y agresión permite diseñar intervenciones que fomenten estrategias adaptativas y reduzcan la violencia, ofreciendo una base empírica sólida para la prevención y el tratamiento de conductas agresivas en contextos clínicos y comunitarios.
stories.paperTitle: Emotion Regulation and Aggression: A Systematic Review and Meta‐Analysis
stories.originalAbstract: ABSTRACT Research on emotion regulation (ER) and aggression has increased rapidly in the past years, but heterogeneity across studies make integration of findings challenging. To estimate the size and consistency of the relationship between ER and aggression we conducted a systematic review and meta‐analysis. In total, 16,369 articles were retrieved from Scopus, PubMed, PsycINFO, and CINAHL, and 137 articles (171 studies) provided 918 effect sizes from a total sample of N = 252,605. Multilevel models showed significant pooled relationships, with small‐to‐moderate effects. Use of adaptive strategies was associated with lower aggression ( r = −0.090, I 2 = 78%), but the precision estimate test (PET) bias corrected effect was non‐significant. Use of maladaptive strategies ( r = 0.329, I 2 = 93%), and difficulties regulating emotions ( r = 0.248, I 2 = 89%), were associated with higher aggression. P‐ curves suggested little evidence of selective reporting while cumulative meta‐analysis showed relatively consistent effects over time. Moderator analyses showed that effects were generally stronger for physical and other forms of aggression than sexual aggression, and weaker for intimate partner targets than other targets. Difficulties in ER were most strongly related to reactive compared with proactive aggression, but the use of ER strategies did not differ between motivations. Our findings suggest that interventions targeting ER, including those that explore and challenge angry predispositions and provide skills to manage impulse control, may help to prevent aggressive behaviour.

stories.hook: ¿Puede el insomnio predecir depresión y ansiedad?
stories.headline: Los trastornos del sueño duplican el riesgo de depresión y ansiedad
stories.finding: Los estudios revisados indican que el insomnio y la corta duración del sueño predicen la aparición de depresión y ansiedad, con odds ratios aproximados de 2 a 3. Además, la evidencia sugiere que intervenciones como la terapia cognitivo-conductual para el insomnio mejoran estos trastornos.
stories.takeaway: Identificar y tratar el insomnio temprano podría prevenir la aparición de trastornos del ánimo, ofreciendo una estrategia preventiva de bajo costo y alta efectividad en la práctica clínica.
stories.paperTitle: The Role of Sleep Disturbances in Depression and Anxiety: A Literature Review
stories.journal: Journal of Education Health and Sport
stories.originalAbstract: Background. Sleep disturbances are among the most frequent comorbid symptoms of mood and anxiety disorders. Contemporary evidence indicates they are robust predictors and likely contributory factors in the onset, maintenance, and relapse of these conditions. Objective. To review and synthesize contemporary evidence on the associations between sleep disturbances and depression and anxiety, focusing on epidemiological data, mechanistic insights, and treatment implications. Methods. A narrative review was conducted using PubMed and PMC databases, covering the years 2011–2025. Keywords included sleep disturbance, insomnia, circadian rhythm, depression, and anxiety. Preference was given to meta-analyses, longitudinal studies, and randomized controlled trials (RCTs). Results. Sleep problems, especially insomnia and short sleep duration, predict the onset of depression and anxiety, with odds ratios of approximately 2–3. Disturbances are bidirectionally linked with mood disorders through mechanisms such as hyperarousal, dysregulated circadian rhythms, altered neurotransmission, and inflammation. Interventions improving sleep—especially cognitive-behavioural therapy for insomnia (CBT-I) and digital CBT-I—produce small to moderate reductions in depressive and anxiety symptoms. Conclusions. Sleep disturbances are not merely symptoms of psychiatric illness but modifiable risk factors and therapeutic targets. Integrating sleep-focused assessment and intervention into mental health and primary care can improve clinical outcomes and possibly prevent new-onset depression or anxiety.

stories.hook: ¿Puede la terapia existencial mejorar la esperanza en pacientes con cáncer avanzado?
stories.headline: Terapia existencial adaptada reduce desesperanza y aumenta sentido de vida
stories.finding: En un estudio cuasi‑experimental con 60 mujeres con cáncer metastásico, el programa de Terapia Cognitiva Existencial mejoró significativamente la autonomía, el propósito de vida, el significado espiritual y disminuyó la desesperanza, mientras el grupo de control no mostró cambios relevantes.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo sugiere que integrar estrategias de aceptación dentro de una intervención culturalmente adaptada puede potenciar el bienestar psicológico al final de la vida, ofreciendo una herramienta clínica valiosa para pacientes con cáncer avanzado.
stories.paperTitle: EXISTENTIAL HEALING AT THE END OF LIFE: A CULTURALLY ADAPTED INTERVENTION FOR TURKISH WOMEN WITH ADVANCED CANCER
stories.originalAbstract: This quasi experimental study assessed the effectiveness of a 12 week Existential Based Cognitive Therapy (EBCT) program for women with metastatic cancer in Türkiye. Sixty participants were allocated to either the intervention or waitlist control group. The intervention integrated meaning centered exercises, symbolic expression, self compassion, and acceptance strategies within culturally congruent therapeutic frameworks. Outcomes were evaluated using validated Turkish versions of the Ryff Psychological Well Being Scale, FACIT Sp 12, and Beck Hopelessness Scale at baseline, mid intervention, and post intervention. Results showed that the EBCT group experienced statistically and clinically significant improvements across all outcome measures—particularly in autonomy, purpose in life, spiritual meaning, and reductions in hopelessness—while the control group displayed no meaningful change. Thematic analysis of anonymized session reflections provided illustrative context for participants’ experiences, highlighting culturally embedded meanings of illness, gendered caregiving roles, and spiritual coping frameworks. Findings suggest that EBCT, when culturally adapted to integrate existential themes with local meaning systems, can promote psychological and spiritual well being among women confronting life limiting illness. This study contributes to death studies literature by demonstrating how existentially grounded psychosocial interventions may support adaptive functioning in non Western settings confronting the existential challenges of advanced cancer.

stories.hook: ¿Puede la compasión superar la vergüenza interna?
stories.headline: La vergüenza internalizada predice negativamente el florecimiento en estudiantes de posgrado
stories.finding: En una muestra de 53 estudiantes de psicología, la vergüenza internalizada mostró una correlación negativa fuerte con el florecimiento (r = -0.67) y, en regresión múltiple, fue el único predictor único significativo (β = -0.64, p < 0.001, R² = 0.45). Además, la ansiedad y evitación del apego también se relacionaron negativamente con el florecimiento (r = -0.35 y -0.33, respectivamente).
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo sugiere que intervenir sobre la vergüenza mediante técnicas de compasión y autoaceptación puede potenciar el florecimiento y la autoestima en estudiantes, ofreciendo una vía clínica eficaz para mejorar su bienestar psicológico.
stories.paperTitle: The burden of shame: mediating attachment and flourishing in psychodynamic training programs
stories.originalAbstract: Introduction: Graduate student burnout and mental health struggles have received much attention; however, there has been less focus on graduate student flourishing and the impact of attachment dimensions and internalized shame. Psychodynamic theorists emphasize the importance of addressing shame, as it often influences well-being and interferes with openness and vulnerability. Materials and methods: The current exploratory study explored flourishing in a sample of 53 graduate students enrolled in two Mid-Atlantic psychodynamically oriented professional psychology programs. Participants completed the Experiences in Close Relationships Scale–Short Form (ECR-S), Flourishing Index (FI), and Internalized Shame Scale (ISS). Statistical analyses included Pearson correlations, multiple regression, and path analysis. Results: Pearson correlations revealed that flourishing was significantly negatively related to attachment anxiety (r = −0.35), attachment avoidance (r = −0.33), and internalized shame (r = −0.67). In a simultaneous multiple regression, internalized shame was the only significant unique predictor of flourishing (β = −0.64, p < 0.001; R2 = 0.45). A path analysis revealed that attachment anxiety (β = 0.35) and avoidance (β = 0.42) had significant direct effects on shame, which in turn predicted reduced flourishing (β = −0.64); the indirect effects of anxiety (β = −0.23, p = 0.008) and avoidance (β = −0.27, p = 0.006) on flourishing through shame were significant, whereas the direct effects of attachment on flourishing were not. Conclusions: Results highlight the importance of shame when examining graduate student flourishing and that attachment may relate to well-being through shame-based mechanisms. Self-report measures and sample size are discussed as limitations. Implications for future research, programmatic intervention, and training are addressed.

stories.hook: ¿Puede la identidad profesional proteger contra el burnout?
stories.headline: La identidad profesional modera el vínculo entre autoeficacia y burnout
stories.finding: En una muestra de 588 docentes de educación física infantil, la autoeficacia mostró una asociación indirecta con el burnout a través de un dominio negativo de fatiga por compasión. Además, la identidad profesional moderó la relación directa, intensificando o atenuando el efecto según su nivel.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo sugiere que fortalecer la identidad profesional y la autoeficacia puede ser una estrategia preventiva contra el burnout en docentes de educación física infantil.
stories.paperTitle: Self-efficacy and job burnout among early childhood physical education teachers: exploratory indirect associations through the negative compassion-fatigue domain and professional identity moderation
stories.originalAbstract: Background Early childhood physical education teachers work at the intersection of early childhood education and physical education, yet psychological factors associated with job burnout in this group remain underexamined. Guided by the Job Demands–Resources model, this study examined associations among self-efficacy, an exploratory negative-domain composite, professional identity, and job burnout, including an indirect association and moderation of the direct association. Methods A cross-sectional online survey using snowball sampling included 588 early childhood physical education teachers in Chengdu, China (555 women, 33 men; mean age = 26.12 years, SD = 5.77). Participants completed the Chinese short-form Teachers’ Sense of Efficacy Scale, an adapted 15-item Chinese compassion-fatigue questionnaire, the Chinese Maslach Burnout Inventory-Education Survey, and the Teacher Professional Identity Scale. An exploratory 10-item negative-domain composite was constructed from five burnout-related and five secondary traumatic stress (STS) items, excluding the five compassion-satisfaction items. Pearson correlations and PROCESS Models 4 and 5 were estimated, adjusting for age and gender. Indirect associations were evaluated using 5,000 bootstrap resamples. Results Self-efficacy was negatively correlated with job burnout (r = −0.38, p < 0.001) and positively correlated with the negative-domain composite (r = 0.16, p < 0.001), which was also positively correlated with job burnout (r = 0.19, p < 0.001). The adjusted indirect association through the composite was positive (ab = 0.081, 95% CI [0.034, 0.143]) and opposed the negative direct association (B = −0.778, p < 0.001). Professional identity moderated the direct association (interaction B = −0.263, p < 0.001; ΔR 2 = 0.018), which was nonsignificant at low professional identity (B = −0.086, 95% CI [−0.260, 0.088]) and strongest at high professional identity (B = −0.422, 95% CI [−0.610, −0.234]). Conclusion Higher self-efficacy was associated with lower job burnout, and this negative association was stronger at higher levels of professional identity. The positive indirect association through the exploratory negative-domain composite was small and sensitive to its operationalization. Given the cross-sectional design and measurement limitations, these findings should be interpreted as exploratory statistical associations rather than evidence of causal mechanisms.

stories.hook: ¿Por qué algunos solteros prosperan mientras otros sufren?
stories.headline: Los solteros se agrupan en cuatro perfiles de apego con distintas vivencias
stories.finding: En dos estudios con 482 y 400 adultos solteros, el análisis de perfiles latentes reveló cuatro grupos de apego: seguro, ansioso, evitativo y temeroso‑evitativo. Estos perfiles mostraron diferencias significativas en la experiencia de la soltería y en indicadores de bienestar psicosocial, evidenciando la heterogeneidad del colectivo de solteros.
stories.takeaway: Reconocer la diversidad de estilos de apego entre solteros permite diseñar intervenciones psicológicas personalizadas que mejoren su bienestar y reduzcan riesgos de aislamiento, ofreciendo una guía más precisa para terapeutas y profesionales de la salud mental.
stories.paperTitle: Diversity in singlehood experiences: Testing an attachment theory model of sub‐groups of singles
stories.originalAbstract: OBJECTIVE: Relationship science has developed several theories to explain how and why people enter and maintain satisfying relationships. Less is known about why some people remain single, despite increasing rates of singlehood throughout the world. Using one of the most widely studied and robust theories-attachment theory-we aim to identify distinct sub-groups of singles and examine whether these sub-groups differ in their experience of singlehood and psychosocial outcomes. METHOD: Across two studies of single adults (Ns = 482 and 400), we used latent profile analysis (LPA) to identify distinct sub-groups of singles. RESULTS: Both studies revealed four distinct profiles consistent with attachment theory: (1) secure; (2) anxious; (3) avoidant; and (4) fearful-avoidant. Furthermore, the four sub-groups of singles differed in theoretically distinct ways in their experience of singlehood and on indicators of psychosocial well-being. CONCLUSIONS: These findings suggest that singles are a heterogeneous group of individuals that can be meaningfully differentiated based on individual differences in attachment security.

stories.hook: ¿Puede la IA reemplazar la adivinación tradicional?
stories.headline: Usuarios chinos adoptan IA generativa para la adivinación, buscando consuelo psicológico
stories.finding: En entrevistas con 22 usuarios habituales y un análisis de 1.842 publicaciones, se observó que quienes buscan consuelo psicológico son particularmente receptivos a la adivinación basada en IA generativa. Valoran su accesibilidad, conveniencia y eficiencia, aunque perciben una menor mística espiritual.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo muestra cómo la tecnología de IA puede convertirse en un recurso de apoyo emocional, modificando prácticas culturales tradicionales y ofreciendo nuevas vías para intervenciones de bienestar que integren herramientas digitales accesibles.
stories.paperTitle: "Re-Tell the Fortune so I Can Believe It": How Chinese User Communities Engage with and Interpret GenAI-based Fortune-Telling
stories.journal: Proceedings of the ACM on Human-Computer Interaction
stories.originalAbstract: People traditionally divine the future by interpreting natural phenomena as oracular signals, especially in societies adhering to traditional beliefs like China. With the advent of Generative AI (GenAI), people gain access to new ways of probing digital oracles for predicting the future. To understand how people use and interpret GenAI for divination in China, we interviewed 22 participants who habitually use GenAI platforms for fortune-telling, complemented by a three-week digital ethnography with 1,842 community posts. Qualitative analysis showed that people who seek psychological comfort are particularly receptive to GenAI-based decision-making. Users valued GenAI’s accessibility, convenience, and efficiency while perceiving its lack of spiritual mystique. We observed community dynamics forming around GenAI tools, where users reinforce interpretations by sharing and discussing with each other, repeating queries until responses align with expectations. Our work uncovers how AI technologies change the way people and communities engage in traditional cultural practices while yearning for the same goals.

stories.hook: ¿Cómo influye la visión del futuro en el peso corporal?
stories.headline: Perspectiva temporal futura reduce el IMC mediante mayor autocontrol
stories.finding: En una muestra de 920 universitarios chinos, una perspectiva temporal orientada al futuro se asoció negativamente con el índice de masa corporal (β = -0.23), mientras que la perspectiva hedonista presente mostró una asociación positiva (β = 0.18). El autocontrol y el consumo de bebidas azucaradas medieron esa asociación.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo sugiere que fomentar una visión futura y fortalecer el autocontrol puede ser una estrategia preventiva contra el sobrepeso, al reducir la ingesta de azúcares, ofreciendo una guía práctica para intervenciones en salud pública y clínica.
stories.paperTitle: Time Perspective and BMI: The Mediating Roles of Self-Control and Sugar-Sweetened Beverage Consumption
stories.originalAbstract: Objective: This study aims to investigate the associations between future, present-hedonistic, and present-fatalistic time perspectives (TP) and body mass index (BMI) among college students, and to examine whether self-control and sugar-sweetened beverage (SSB) consumption mediate these relationships. Methods: A cross-sectional survey was conducted in Jiangsu Province, China, involving 920 college students. The survey collected data on participants' height, weight, future TP, present-hedonistic TP, present-fatalistic TP, self-control, and SSB consumption. Multiple hierarchical regression analysis was employed to identify potential covariates, and three chain mediation models were analyzed using the PROCESS macro (Model 6) in SPSS version 26. Results: The results indicated that future TP was negatively associated with BMI (β = -0.23, 95% CI = [-3.81, -2.24]), and present-hedonistic TP showed a positive association (β = 0.18, 95% CI = [1.47, 2.73]). Present-fatalistic TP was not significantly related to BMI. Furthermore, self-control and SSB consumption mediated the relationships between future TP, present-hedonistic TP, present-fatalistic TP, and BMI (β = -0.02, 95% CI [-0.04, -0.01]; β = 0.02, 95% CI [0.01, 0.02]); β = 0.02, 95% CI = [0.01, 0.02]). Conclusion: TP, self-control, and SSB consumption are important factors associated with BMI among college students. Promoting a future-oriented TP and self-control, while reducing present-oriented TP and SSB intake, may support more effective BMI management. These findings offer theoretical implications for designing targeted health interventions.

stories.hook: ¿Puede la terapia transdiagnóstica fortalecer la resiliencia materna?
stories.headline: Terapia emocional transdiagnóstica reduce evitamiento cognitivo y aumenta hardiness en madres en duelo
stories.finding: En un estudio cuasi‑experimental con 30 madres que habían perdido a su hijo, el grupo experimental recibió doce sesiones semanales de terapia emocional transdiagnóstica. Comparado con el grupo control sin intervención, mostró una disminución del evitamiento cognitivo y un aumento significativo de la hardiness psicológica.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo sugiere que la terapia emocional transdiagnóstica puede ser una herramienta eficaz para promover la resiliencia y reducir estrategias de evitación en madres en duelo, ofreciendo una opción clínica basada en evidencia para el acompañamiento del duelo infantil.
stories.paperTitle: The Effectiveness of Emotion-Focused Transdiagnostic Therapy on Cognitive Avoidance and Psychological Hardiness in Mothers with the Experience of Child Loss
stories.journal: International Journal of Education and Cognitive Sciences
stories.originalAbstract: Purpose: The present study aimed to examine the effectiveness of emotion-focused transdiagnostic therapy in reducing cognitive avoidance and increasing psychological hardiness in bereaved mothers. Methods and Materials: In terms of purpose, this was an applied study, and in terms of implementation, it was a quasi-experimental study with a pretest–posttest control-group design and a two-month follow-up phase. The statistical population included all mothers with the experience of child loss residing in Tehran in 2025 who had referred to counseling centers, psychotherapy clinics, health centers, and grief-related support associations. Using purposive and convenience sampling, 30 individuals who met the inclusion criteria were selected and, after providing informed consent, were randomly assigned to an experimental group (15 participants) and a control group (15 participants). The experimental group received emotion-focused transdiagnostic therapy in twelve weekly 60-minute sessions, whereas the control group received no intervention. The research instruments included the Cognitive Avoidance Questionnaire (Sexton & Dugas, 2008) and the Psychological Hardiness Scale (Kobasa, 1979), which were administered at the pretest, posttest, and follow-up stages. The data were analyzed using repeated-measures analysis of variance and SPSS version 27. Findings: The results showed that emotion-focused transdiagnostic therapy significantly reduced cognitive avoidance and increased psychological hardiness in the experimental group (p < .001). Moreover, the effectiveness of the therapy was maintained at the follow-up stage, and the difference between the posttest and follow-up scores was not significant. Conclusion: Emotion-focused transdiagnostic therapy can be an effective approach for improving emotional adjustment in bereaved mothers by reducing cognitive avoidance and strengthening psychological hardiness. It is recommended that this therapeutic model be used in grief-related supportive and clinical programs.

stories.hook: ¿Influye la cultura en los déficits ejecutivos del TDAH?
stories.headline: Niños chinos con TDAH presentan peor control inhibitorio y memoria de trabajo
stories.finding: En una muestra de 102 niños con TDAH y 96 controles típicos de China y Australia, se aplicó la misma batería neuropsicológica. Los niños chinos con TDAH obtuvieron puntuaciones significativamente menores en control inhibitorio y memoria de trabajo respecto a sus pares chinos, patrón ausente en los australianos.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo sugiere que los déficits ejecutivos del TDAH pueden variar según el contexto cultural, lo que implica que las intervenciones deben adaptarse a factores socioculturales para ser efectivas.
stories.paperTitle: Cross‐cultural variations in executive function impairments among children with attention deficit/hyperactivity disorder
stories.originalAbstract: Background: Executive function (EF) impairments are heterogeneous in children with attention deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD). Culture has a significant impact on EF development in typically developing (TD) children, yet its influence on EF impairments in those with ADHD remains understudied. This study aims to investigate the impact of cultural factors on EF impairments in children with ADHD through a cross-cultural comparison. Methods: To ensure a robust sample size, the study initially recruited a large participant pool of 690 children from China and Australia. We applied similar diagnostic criteria and used propensity score matching to align clinical representation. This approach resulted in a final sample of 198 children aged 7-12, including 102 children diagnosed with ADHD and 96 TD peers. The same neuropsychological testing battery was used to assess EF in terms of working memory (WM), inhibitory control (IC), and set shifting. Results: Significant cultural effects were observed: Chinese children with ADHD showed lower performance in IC and WM compared to their TD peers, a pattern not seen in Australian children. A latent profile analysis revealed distinct EF profiles, highlighting a subgroup of Chinese children with severe EF impairments. Conclusions: This study advances cross-cultural ADHD research on EF by using a robust methodology, including consistent diagnostic and testing procedures, propensity score matching, and person-centered analysis. Our findings suggest that high-EF-expectation environments may have a negative effect on EF in children with ADHD, which provides insight into the underlying contributors to heterogeneous EF and underscores the need for culturally tailored ADHD interventions.

stories.hook: ¿Cómo protege la resiliencia a los adolescentes?
stories.headline: Resiliencia atenúa el impacto del rechazo paternal en problemas emocionales
stories.finding: En un estudio transversal con 895 adolescentes chinos (10‑18 años), se observó que el estilo de crianza de rechazo paternal se asoció a mayores problemas emocionales y conductuales (EBP media = 12,71 ± 5,77). El análisis de mediación mostró que la resiliencia mediaba parcialmente esta relación (a × b = 0,051, IC 95 % BCa).
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo sugiere que fortalecer la resiliencia en adolescentes puede reducir los efectos nocivos de estilos de crianza negativos, ofreciendo una vía práctica para intervenciones preventivas en salud mental.
stories.paperTitle: Effect of parenting style on the emotional and behavioral problems among Chinese adolescents: the mediating effect of resilience
stories.originalAbstract: BACKGROUND: Although previous studies have found that parenting style significantly predicts emotional and behavioral problems (EBPs) among Chinese adolescents, the mechanism between different parenting styles and EBPs requires in-depth investigation. In our study, we aimed to investigate the mediating effect of resilience, a positive psychological characteristic, between parenting style and EBPs among Chinese adolescents. METHODS: In this cross-sectional study, we used a multistage stratified cluster random sampling method to collect data in Shenyang, Liaoning Province from November to December 2019. Self-developed questionnaires were distributed to 1028 adolescents aged 10-18. Finally, the study consisted of 895 participants. The bootstrap method was used to investigate the role of resilience as a mediator in the relationship between different parenting styles and EBPs from a positive psychology perspective. RESULTS: The mean score of EBPs was 12.71 (SD = 5.77). After controlling for variables such as gender, age, left-behind children, family type and family income, resilience partially played a mediating role in the associations of paternal rejection (a × b = 0.051 BCa95%CI:0.023,0.080), maternal rejection (a × b = 0.055 BCa95%CI: 0.024, 0.086), paternal emotional warmth (a × b = -0.139 BCa95%CI: -0.182, -0.099) and maternal emotional warmth (a × b = -0.140 BCa95%CI: -0.182, -0.102), with EBPs. The effect sizes were11.28%, 11.51%, 40.76%, and 38.78%, respectively. CONCLUSIONS: Resilience could partially mediate the relationship between parenting style and EBPs, highlighting that parents should adopt a positive parenting style and that resilience improvement could be effective in reducing EBPs among Chinese adolescents.

stories.hook: ¿Puede el ejercicio prevenir el deterioro neurodegenerativo?
stories.headline: El ejercicio potencia neuroplasticidad y reduce riesgos de enfermedades neurodegenerativas
stories.finding: El ejercicio estimula la neuroplasticidad mediante señalización neurotrófica (BDNF, IGF‑1, VEGF), regulación neuroendocrina, epigenética y metabolismo, favoreciendo neurogénesis hipocampal, mayor plasticidad sináptica y mejor conectividad cerebral. También reduce la agregación proteica, la excitotoxicidad y el estrés oxidativo, procesos implicados en Alzheimer y Parkinson.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo respalda el uso del ejercicio como intervención no farmacológica para preservar la función cognitiva y retrasar la aparición de enfermedades neurodegenerativas, ofreciendo una estrategia accesible y de bajo costo para la prevención y el manejo clínico.
stories.paperTitle: Exercise-Induced Neuroplasticity: Adaptive Mechanisms and Preventive Potential in Neurodegenerative Disorders
stories.originalAbstract: Background/Objectives: Neurodegenerative diseases represent a growing global health challenge with limited therapeutic options. Physical exercise has emerged as a promising non-pharmacological intervention with potential neuroprotective effects. This narrative review examines the mechanisms through which exercise induces neuroplasticity and their implications for neurodegenerative disease prevention. Methods: We synthesized evidence from molecular, animal, and human studies on exercise-induced neuroplasticity and neurodegenerative disease prevention through a comprehensive literature review. Results: Exercise enhances neuroplasticity through multiple pathways: (1) neurotrophic signaling (BDNF, IGF-1, VEGF), (2) neuroendocrine regulation, (3) epigenetic modifications, and (4) metabolic pathway optimization. These molecular changes support structural adaptations including hippocampal neurogenesis, enhanced synaptic plasticity, improved cerebrovascular function, and optimized brain network connectivity. Exercise directly impacts pathological features of neurodegenerative diseases by reducing protein aggregation, attenuating excitotoxicity and oxidative stress, and enhancing mitochondrial function. Clinical evidence consistently demonstrates associations between physical activity and reduced neurodegenerative risk, with intervention studies supporting causal benefits on cognitive function and brain structure. Conclusions: Exercise represents a multi-target intervention addressing several pathological mechanisms simultaneously across various neurodegenerative conditions. Its accessibility, minimal side effects, and multiple health benefits position it as a promising preventive strategy. Future research should focus on understanding individual response variability, developing sensitive biomarkers, and creating personalized exercise prescriptions for optimal neuroprotection.
stories.abstract: Background/Objectives: Neurodegenerative diseases represent a growing global health challenge with limited therapeutic options. Physical exercise has emerged as a promising non-pharmacological intervention with potential neuroprotective effects. This narrative review examines the mechanisms through which exercise induces neuroplasticity and their implications for neurodegenerative disease prevention. Methods: We synthesized evidence from molecular, animal, and human studies on exercise-induced neuroplasticity and neurodegenerative disease prevention through a comprehensive literature review. Results: Exercise enhances neuroplasticity through multiple pathways: (1) neurotrophic signaling (BDNF, IGF-1, VEGF), (2) neuroendocrine regulation, (3) epigenetic modifications, and (4) metabolic pathway optimization. These molecular changes support structural adaptations including hippocampal neurogenesis, enhanced synaptic plasticity, improved cerebrovascular function, and optimized brain network connectivity. Exercise directly impacts pathological features of neurodegenerative diseases by reducing protein aggregation, attenuating excitotoxicity and oxidative stress, and enhancing mitochondrial function. Clinical evidence consistently demonstrates associations between physical activity and reduced neurodegenerative risk, with intervention studies supporting causal benefits on cognitive function and brain structure. Conclusions: Exercise represents a multi-target intervention addressing several pathological mechanisms simultaneously across various neurodegenerative conditions. Its accessibility, minimal side effects, and multiple health benefits position it as a promising preventive strategy. Future research should focus on understanding individual response variability, developing sensitive biomarkers, and creating personalized exercise prescriptions for optimal neuroprotection.
